name: Austin
tagline: Keep it weird, keep it easy
description: A spring-fed, guitar-strung sprawl where the barbecue smoke, the swimming holes, and the live music never really quit. Come for the food-truck lines and the bat flights, stay because nobody here is in a hurry to be anything but themselves.

hero.summer: Heat like a wet quilt — so we do what Austin's always done: slide into 68-degree Barton Springs, float the lake till dusk, and let the smoke rise cooler come nightfall.
hero.fall: The light goes gold, the patios fill, and ACL guitars drift clear across Zilker — this is the season Austin was built for, and everybody knows it.
hero.winter: Mild and easy, brisket steam curling into the cool, breakfast tacos steady, the trails and the bats-adjacent quiet all ours while the crowds thin out.
hero.spring: Bluebonnets on the Hill Country roadsides and the whole world showing up for SXSW — loud, kinetic, and gloriously overstuffed, the way we like it once a year.

nexus.anchor: Barton Springs Pool & Lady Bird Lake
nexus.radius: Zilker Park & the Lady Bird Lake hike-and-bike loop, roughly 3 miles of downtown-hugging waterfront
nexus.description: Everything in Austin bends back toward the water. Barton Springs is a 68-degree limestone-fed pool that never changes temperature, and Lady Bird Lake wraps the downtown skyline in a 10-mile loop of trail, paddlers, and — at dusk from March to fall — 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats pouring out from under Congress Avenue Bridge. Cool off first, then the barbecue, the bars, and the music all make sense.

nexus_grid.title: Barton Springs Pool
nexus_grid.description: Three acres of spring-fed limestone pool holding a steady 68 degrees year-round. The great equalizer — everybody floats here.

nexus_grid.title: The Butler Trail
nexus_grid.description: The 10-mile hike-and-bike loop around Lady Bird Lake, skyline on one side, paddleboarders on the other. Free and always open.

nexus_grid.title: Congress Bridge Bats
nexus_grid.description: North America's largest urban bat colony spirals out at dusk from spring through fall. The best free show in town — bring patience and a spot on the bridge.

nexus_grid.title: The Barbecue Tier
nexus_grid.description: The lines are the ritual. Post oak smoke, salt-and-pepper brisket, and a wait that's part of the meal. Show up early, stay humble.

nexus_grid.title: East Austin Murals & Bars
nexus_grid.description: East of I-35, the walls talk — heritage murals, taco trucks, dive patios, and the deepest cultural roots in the city, from the Chitlin' Circuit onward.

nexus_grid.title: Hill Country Wineries
nexus_grid.description: Roll west out of town into bluebonnet-and-limestone country for Texas wine, peach stands, and Fredericksburg's German main street.

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: Chase the smoke. Brisket by the pound, breakfast tacos by the dozen, and food-truck courts where the best meal of your trip costs twelve bucks.

modes.label: Chill
modes.description: Austin's default speed. A float on the lake, a shady patio, a cold Topo Chico, and absolutely nowhere you need to be.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Sunset paddle on the lake, a two-top on a candlelit East Side patio, and the skyline going pink over the water.

modes.label: Adventurer
modes.description: Barton Creek Greenbelt trails, cliff jumps into the springs, kayak the lake, then a day-trip into Hill Country canyon country.

modes.label: Music
modes.description: The Live Music Capital earns it nightly. Red River clubs, South Congress stages, honky-tonks, and a heritage that runs from Victory Grill to Armadillo World HQ.

modes.label: Nightlife
modes.description: Rainey Street bungalow bars, Sixth Street chaos, East Side cocktail dens, and rooftops that don't call last round early.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: Splash pads and spring pools, the bat show, the Thinkery, Zilker's train and trails — Austin's easy on kids and easier on parents.

transit.from_nearest_hub: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) sits about 8 miles southeast of downtown, roughly 15-25 minutes by car depending on traffic. The Capital Metro Rapid 20 bus and rideshare both run the airport-to-downtown corridor.
transit.local_transport: A car makes the sprawl and the Hill Country day-trips easy, but downtown, South Congress, Rainey, and the East Side are walkable and bike-friendly. CapMetro runs buses, the MetroRapid lines, and a single Red Line commuter rail; rideshare and rentable e-scooters/bikes fill the gaps. The Lady Bird Lake trail connects much of the central core on foot.

side_trips.name: Lockhart
side_trips.pitch: The Barbecue Capital of Texas, and it isn't close. Four legendary smokehouses in one small courthouse town — this is the pilgrimage serious eaters make.

side_trips.name: Fredericksburg
side_trips.pitch: German Hill Country roots, a walkable Main Street of biergartens and shops, and the gateway to Texas Wine Country's Highway 290 tasting corridor.
highlights: National Museum of the Pacific War

concierge.name: The Armadillo
concierge.greeting: Well hey there, welcome to Austin — pull up, take a breath, you made it. I'm the Armadillo, named for the old World Headquarters where this town learned to be gloriously itself. Whatcha hungry for — brisket, a swim, or a little live music?
concierge.personality: Keep-it-weird warm, patient as a food-truck line on a Saturday, zero pretension. Talks slow, points true, treats a first-timer and a fifth-gen local exactly the same. Knows the smoke's worth the wait and the water's worth the drive.
concierge.sign_off: Now go get in the springs before it gets hot — I'll keep your spot in line. Stay weird out there.
